name: Out-of-bounds Read
principle: Code reads from an array, pointer, or string using an index, offset, or length that can fall outside the intended buffer. This can disclose adjacent memory, reveal addresses for later exploitation, or crash the process.
detection_signals: array[index] read guarded only by index < len with no index >= 0 check
buf[offset] or *(buf + offset) where offset is input-derived and not checked against buffer size
for/while loop reads buf[i] while i < untrusted_len without untrusted_len <= actual_buf_size
memcpy(dst, src, len), memmove(dst, src, len), write(fd, src, len), or send(fd, src, len) where len can exceed src buffer size
strlen(buf), printf("%s", buf), strcpy(dst, buf), or strcmp(buf, x) on a buffer that may lack a NUL within its allocated size
C++ vector/string operator[] read with external index and no prior range check
negative_signals: read guarded by index >= 0 && index < len where len is the actual element count
offset checked with offset <= size && read_len <= size - offset before pointer read
length clamped with len = min(requested_len, actual_buf_size) before memcpy/send/write source read
bounded string scan uses strnlen(buf, buf_size) or memchr(buf, '\0', buf_size) before treating buf as a C string
C++ read uses vector::at() or string::at() and exception is handled without exposing memory
false_defense_traps: Checking only index < len misses negative index under-read
Trusting protocol or struct length fields without comparing to received buffer size
Relying on a NUL sentinel in untrusted or fixed-size input
Casting a signed index to size_t before validation hides negative values as huge positives
Assuming out-of-bounds read is only DoS; leaked addresses or secrets can aid later attacks
verification_focus: Can every read index, pointer offset, and read length be proven within the intended buffer bounds at the read site?

consequence_chains.trigger: out-of-range pointer offset is dereferenced for reading
consequence_chains.consequence: read before or after the buffer, causing memory disclosure or crash

consequence_chains.trigger: untrusted pointer is dereferenced for reading without validating object bounds
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker-controlled address range may be read

consequence_chains.trigger: out-of-bounds bytes contain secrets, PII, keys, or memory addresses
consequence_chains.consequence: sensitive information exposure and possible ASLR bypass

patch_principle: Validate lower and upper bounds before every indexed or pointer-based read
Compare untrusted length fields against the actual buffer size before loops or bulk reads
Use bounded string APIs and do not depend on untrusted sentinel termination
Prefer memory-safe containers or checked accessors where practical
